title: The Pathologist: Preparing Pathology for the Cancer Surge
summary: As U.S. cancer diagnoses are expected to exceed 2 million cases annually, The Pathologist spoke with Shakti Ramkissoon, senior vice president of enterprise oncology at Labcorp, about why digital pathology is critical to meeting the surge.
body_markdown:
As U.S. cancer diagnoses are expected to exceed 2 million cases annually,[The Pathologist](https://thepathologist.com/issues/2026/articles/october/preparing-pathology-for-the-cancer-surge/) spoke with Shakti Ramkissoon, senior vice president of enterprise oncology at Labcorp, about why digital pathology is critical to meeting the surge.


**Key takeaway:** Earlier cancer detection saves lives but is dramatically increasing the volume and complexity of pathology work, requiring labs to adopt digital tools and integrated diagnostic approaches to keep pace.


"Early detection does not simply mean more specimens," Ramkissoon told *The Pathologist* . "It means more complex diagnostic workups."


The role of the pathologist is evolving to combine traditional morphology with molecular profiling, germline testing and other investigations, then synthesize those findings into clear, actionable reports for oncologists and patients.


**Why it matters:** The coming cancer surge places unprecedented pressure on an already strained laboratory workforce. Labcorp's emphasis on digital pathology and integrated diagnostics reflects a broader industry shift, equipping pathologists to handle rising case volumes and complexity while keeping patient care at the center of the diagnostic pathway.


**Read the full article in**[The Pathologist](https://thepathologist.com/issues/2026/articles/october/preparing-pathology-for-the-cancer-surge/) **.**
